$Comment: Rivet Guard (DESIGN.md 6.1, 6.2): a shield bearer, copied from vanilla Template_Dungeon_Goblin_Guardian and changed as tools/models/heartworks/rivet_guard.role.mjs explains. Trash mob of the Heartworks: stands sentry until aggroed, rallies robots within 5 blocks.

Instructions.$Comment: Scale health to the party size on first aggro (the dungeon goblins' tiers: x1.55, x2.1, x2.65).
Round 5: reset the charge timer and the latches between fights (vanilla Template_Dungeon_Goblin_Mace resets its slam the same way).
Aggro on any attacker, at any range or without line of sight.
Standard detection: hear the robots' rally beacon, see or hear nearby hostiles. Crouching players are not heard.
Stand sentry until aggroed. Every 6 to 14 s: look about, polish the shield, or vent the stack.
Alerted clip: the head snaps up, the shield comes up.
Switch to combat if attacked.
Watch the target and switch to combat after a moment.
No target: back to standing sentry.
Swap to a closer target when there is one.
Watch the target when detected; turn slowly behind the shield, quickly without it.

Arm the shield-charge timer once per fight (a flag, not Once: state changes clear Once sensors). First charge 2 s in, then every ChargeCooldownRange. As vanilla Template_Dungeon_Goblin_Mace arms its slam.

Actions.$Comment: Pin the first charge delay (TimerRestart rolls the cooldown range).
Actions.Name: Charge_Ready

Instructions.$Comment: Call the robots: once a fight, when its shield breaks or it falls below 60% health, it vents its stack and whistles. Coglings within CallRange that hear the Flock_Attack beacon come running at its target; other robots get the rally. Latched by Call_Active so the blocking list survives its own sensor changing.

Shield charge: with the shield up and the target 5 to 10 blocks off in sight, it closes the distance (Root_Machinaria_Heartworks_Rivet_Guard_Shield_Charge: 0.7 s wind-up, dash, 0.7 s recovery). Every ChargeCooldownRange. Latched by Charge_Active, as vanilla Template_Dungeon_Goblin_Mace latches its slam.
Start the guard cycle timer: guard first, then a mace window after each guard.
Hold shield distance while ready to guard, circling the target behind the shield (round 5 note 7).
Close to mace distance in the mace window.
Mace distance once buckled.

Plate Buckled: stamina broken while the shield is still in the off hand (vanilla Dungeon_Goblin_Guardian: "Remove the off-hand shield when stamina is broken"). The shield leaves the hand for good and the Buckled effect adds sparks; the guard interaction plays the 1.2 s stagger. All in one tick, not blocking: unequipping ends its own sensor.
Hit while ready (an arrow from afar, a blow from close): guard at once.
Guard at medium range when ready: 1, 1.5 or 2 s behind the shield, the bash, then the mace window.
The mace window with the shield up: the two-hit chain.
Buckled: the mace alone, faster.
Otherwise chase (target loss is handled there).
Rally every robot within 5 blocks with the locked target, then fight.
Chase the target.

NameTranslationKey.Description: Translation key for NPC name display

MaxHealth.Description: Max health for the NPC (round 2 note 22: tankier than the goblins; the Deepworks Dungeon_Goblin_Guardian has 90, the Dungeon_Goblin_Mace 160)

DeathAnimationTime.Description: Seconds the felled guard lies before it goes

LeashDistance.Description: Distance from the leash point before the NPC wants to return home

LeashMinPlayerDistance.Description: The NPC will not give up the chase while the player is closer than this

LeashTimer.Description: Seconds beyond leash range, without damage or a close player, before the NPC returns home

HardLeashDistance.Description: Absolute maximum distance from the leash point before the NPC returns home unconditionally

ViewRange.Description: The view range of the NPC

ViewSector.Description: The view sector of the NPC

HearingRange.Description: The hearing range of the NPC

AbsoluteDetectionRange.Description: The range at which an entity is guaranteed to be detected

WanderRadius.Description: The search radius of the NPC

AlertedRange.Description: The alerted range of the NPC

AlertedTimeout.Description: The time range after which an NPC will transition from alerted to combat

CombatMessageRange.Description: The range at which the NPC will send combat messages

CombatMessageTargetGroups.Description: The NPC groups the rally is sent to

AttackDistance.Description: The distance the NPC keeps to the target and swings from

ShieldGuardCooldownRange.Description: From the start of a guard to the next: the guard and bash (about 2.5 to 3.5 s), then a 3 to 4 s mace window (DESIGN.md 6.2)

MaceAttackPauseRange.Description: Pause between mace chains with the shield up, counted from the start of the 1.85 s chain (1.5 to 2 s idle)

BuckledMaceAttackPauseRange.Description: Pause between mace chains once buckled, counted from the start (0.75 to 1 s idle)

Block.Description: The guard, which ends in the shield bash

BlockDistance.Description: The distance at which the NPC raises its shield

ShieldChargeAttack.Description: Round 5: the shield charge that closes the distance

ChargeMinDistance.Description: Round 5: the shield charge starts only beyond this distance

ChargeDistance.Description: Round 5: and within this distance (in sight)

ChargeCooldownRange.Description: Round 5: seconds between shield charges (the first comes 2 s into the fight)

CallRange.Description: Round 5: how far its whistle reaches the Coglings and other robots

CallHealthRange.Description: Round 5: health fraction at which it calls the robots (or when its shield breaks), once a fight

StrafingDurationRange.Description: Round 5: how long each circling step behind the shield lasts

StrafingFrequencyRange.Description: Round 5: how often it circles while holding shield distance

CombatMovingRelativeSpeed.Description: The combat speed as relative to max speed

ConfusedTimeRange.Description: The time during which the NPC will be confused

SearchTimeRange.Description: The time during which the NPC will search for a target

MemoriesUnlockedBy.Description: How the player records the memory, either Proximity or Kill.

MemoriesKillRange.Description: Radius in blocks in which the memory is recorded when the NPC dies. 0 uses the server default.
